heroHeadline: Carney and Lutnick Trade Public Blame as Sept 8 Retaliation Deadline Nears
heroSubtitle: With Canada's C$27.6B retaliatory tariffs still on track to take effect Sept 8, the US and Canada spent early September trading blame in public rather than negotiating. Commerce Secretary Lutnick said Sept 3 that Canada invented 'crazy ideas' to walk away from talks for domestic political reasons; PM Carney, speaking from Thunder Bay, rejected the claim — 'appointed, unelected cabinet members in the United States are [not] experts on Canadian politics' — and said US negotiators had shifted their own red-line positions since the Aug 21 collapse. Trump followed with a Truth Social warning that Carney would regret making him 'the enemy.' Carney separately said Sept 1 that US demands aimed to 'wipe out' Canadian industries or turn them into subsidiaries. No new talks are scheduled. In Mexico City, President Sheinbaum said Sept 3 her government was 'working very hard' on a better steel, aluminum and auto deal ahead of a fourth bilateral round, while maintaining Mexico's non-retaliation posture.
